result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, the sync path returns the raw fetch response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, whose payload is only validated against minimumTokenResponseSchema (access_token + a number). But in larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff pipes that response directly into handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log), which expects Lark's nested/documented refresh response shape; a conforming minimal sync response cannot be parsed by it, so Lark credential refresh breaks when sync is enabled. Also unlike google/o365/zoom, no parseRefreshTokenResponse adaptation is applied here

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens() but then passes the response directly to handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either the response from the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT or the result of refreshFunction(). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the sync endpoint returns a minimal token response (access_token + expiry), but handleLarkError expects Lark's nested response structure (RefreshTokenResp). This mismatch means the Lark-specific parsing will fail when credential sharing is enabled, as the sync endpoint's response format won't match Lark's expected nested structure.
